headline: Fanfiction community at war with AI over new detection tool on Archive of Our Own
summary: A new fan-made tool for Archive of Our Own claims to detect AI-generated fanfiction by identifying specific code artifacts, igniting a fierce debate and public shaming within the creative community.
details: A new movement has emerged within fanfiction communities, aiming to identify and root out authors using generative AI. However, the detection methods being implemented are raising questions about their accuracy and potential for misuse.

Distaste for AI tools like Claude and ChatGPT has been prevalent in creative communities. On June 29th, an anonymous X account, @heatedrivalryai, released a "skin" for Archive of Our Own (AO3) to purportedly identify coding artifacts from Anthropic's Claude bot.

The skin works by detecting a specific code, "font-claude-response-body," which Claude injects when text is directly pasted into AO3. If this code is present, the AO3 page background turns red, signaling potential AI generation.

Tests confirm the skin effectively flags text directly pasted from Claude. Despite the creator's intent to demonstrate functionality, fanfic communities have quickly started publicly naming and shaming writers whose works were flagged, fueling mistrust.

Anthropic has not verified the tool's functionality, but independent testing supports its methodology for direct pastes. However, there are significant risks of both false negatives and overgeneralizations regarding AI usage.

The detection method is easily bypassed: the code wrapping is only preserved if text is copied directly from Claude. Any editing in external programs like Google Docs or Microsoft Word before pasting to AO3 will remove the artifacts.

Crucially, the tool doesn't indicate the extent of AI use. A red screen could mean an entire story was AI-generated, or simply that a few human-written sentences were briefly run through Claude for minor edits like spell-checking or translation.

headline_marked: [[Midjourney wants Hollywood studios to show how they use AI]] in legal battle
headline: Midjourney wants Hollywood studios to show how they use AI in legal battle
summary: Midjourney is challenging a judge's ruling, demanding Hollywood studios reveal their full AI business plans, research, training data, and model weights in court.
details: Midjourney is asking the Hollywood studios that sued it to disclose extensive details about their AI operations. This includes their AI business plans, research reports, training datasets, model weights, and even internal presentations about AI used for board meetings.

Previously, in mid-June, a magistrate judge allowed the studios to withhold most of this information, limiting discovery to only "consumer-facing" AI applications. Midjourney is now appealing this decision, asking the federal court to overturn the magistrate judge's order.
